# M0-a-14 — closing check after fix round 1 (lane `check/M0-a-14-close-r1`, flow flow-7, stage group 9, 2026-10-05)

Lane `check/M0-a-14-close-r1` ran under Opus 5.5 in Claude Code on the owner's Windows 11 PC (WSL2 Ubuntu, Linux x64,
Node v24.12.0) on 2026-10-05, from about 12:51 to 13:55. This seat is an implementer-side independent closing checker.
It is not the item's author (`build/M0-a-14`, L-0166), its fixer (`build/M0-a-14-fix1`, L-0178) or its first checker
(`check/M0-a-14`, L-0177). Under J162 and J169, the item's second check closes it.

How the seat worked:

* It changed no file of the item and ran no git command.
* It ran one vitest process at a time: `--maxWorkers=2` for the gates and `--maxWorkers=1` for every mutant, with no
  `--` before a vitest flag (J182). `free -m` showed 9–12 GB available before each run.
* The mutants ran in its own scratch mirror `maps-scratch/waves/check-M0-a-14/close-r1/mirror`. Each mutated source was
  restored after its run, and all eight `src/invariants/*.ts` files were then byte-compared with the tree (`cmp`: all
  the same). The mirror's `node_modules` was deleted afterwards.
* It planned its mutants from the code, §3.10, C-0200 and the first check's failing lines. Its first grep of the lane
  log, run to apply the resume rule, did show the author's CHECKPOINT summary lines. That is recorded in L-0180. It
  opened no `selfcheck-*` folder.

## Verdict: PASS. B1 – B5 are fixed and there is no new blocker

The fix round added eight tests to `fixtures.test.ts` and changed no source file: every `src/invariants/` hash in the
landed record equals the tree. Each of the first check's seven surviving mutants is now killed by the test aimed at it
(CONFIRMED). The seat's own 34 mutants left 16 survivors at first. It then wrote controls X07 – X35 in the mirror. Each
control passes on the real code, so the code's result is right in every case. The controls kill 11 of the survivors,
and those survivors become further hardening tests. Of the other five, two are equivalent or give the same verdict,
and three are contrived. None of the 16 falls under the brief's list of blockers. They are notes 11 – 22 in
`checks/M0-a-14-notes.md`, with ready recipes.

**Kernel gate.** The kernel project gate's first run exited 1 on one test. That test belongs to another item: M0-a-05's
insertChain B-FUZZ, an N-37-class router gap on a random seed that replays deterministically. Its import graph reaches
no file of `src/invariants/`. A re-run passed 1338/1338, exit 0. This is note 23, for the session.

## (3) New findings: none is a blocker

The seat ran 34 mutants of its own (C01 – C35), aimed at §3.10's clauses and C-0200's readings.

* **18 were killed by the item's tests:** C01 – C06, C11 – C14, C16, C17, C27 – C32.
* **11 more were killed only by this seat's controls**, each of which passes on the real code. These are notes 11 – 21:
  C07, C08, C15, C18, C19, C20, C21, C23, C25, C26, C35. Each one is a sub-case of a clause that already has a negative
  control: an edge row beside the tested vertex row, a ring beside the tested open way, absorption beside the tested
  merge, three coarser edges beside the tested pair with different rows, degree 3 beside the tested degree 4, and dead
  face and edge slots beside the tested vertex slot. Two of them (C15 and C25) are guards against over-reporting, which
  no positive fixture exercises. These are further hardening tests, not wrong results.
* **2 are equivalent or give the same verdict:** C33 (`Int32Array` storage) and C22 (the row's guard turns the throw
  into a failure).
* **3 are contrived:** C09, C10 and C34 (notes 13, 14 and 22).

So the brief's blocker list is not met. No gate exits non-zero because of this item. No listed interface or test is
missing. There is no stub or undeclared shortcut. No honest input gets a wrong result. There is no clean-room breach
and no path outside `plat/`.

round needs only new negative fixtures (templates below) and changes no source file. Ten minor notes for M4 are in

## 5 Probes (CONFIRMED, run in the scratch mirror `~/maps-scratch/waves/check-M0-a-14/`)

* **A — placement bound with `placed` handed in.** 16 fuzz seeds, 195 commits. Each batch's new vertices were passed in
  as `placed`. Result: 141 subjects, 0 problems from any hard row.
* **B — nudged vertices.** 300 trials, each moving a vertex by up to ±30 or ±400 cm and re-attaching the index. The
  independent oracles (`allProblems`) broke 17 arenas. The suite missed 0 of them, both batch-local (a record naming the
  vertex as moved, with its faces) and in `checkCI`.
* **C — nested islands.** An L2 ring with an L3 ring inside it, plus a second L3 island: nesting, Euler and the whole
  suite hold, and so do the oracles.
* **Bundle.** `define PLAT_DEBUG_BUILD=false` against `dist/` switches the arena off. Under `plat-source` with
  `sideEffects: false`, `debug.ts` is tree-shaken and the switch stays on. This is note 7, for M1's app bundle.

## 7 Blockers

* **B1 — min-edge.** The negatives use axis-aligned edges only, at 24 and 25 cm. Mutant K02b measures length with the
  L1 norm (`|dx| + |dy| < r`) and survives the whole test set.
  * Control C5: the lane (500, 500)–(1500, 1500) with its end moved to (517, 517), a 24.04 cm diagonal. The row fails on
    the real code and holds under K02b.
  * Required: add a diagonal negative (24.04 cm fails) and a diagonal positive at the bound (for example (0, 0)–(15, 20),
    25 cm, holds).
* **B2 — euler.** The only negative is a rotation swap, which makes V − E + F too small by 2. Mutant K38 flags only
  χ < components (`χ ≠ 1 + c` replaced by `χ < c`) and survives.
  * Control C4: re-link the lower-left L1 block's ring into two cycles by swapping the successors of the half-edges
    entering (0, 0) and (2000, 2000). That gives one face too many, `checkCI` fails euler, and K38 holds.
  * Required: add a negative for a face count that is too high, plus one for a deficit of exactly 1, so that equality
    is pinned in both directions.
* **B3 — references-resolve.** Three §3.10 clauses have no negative.
  * (a) "at least one knot per ring". K31 survives. Control C6: a closed `kerb` ring with a `width_knot` profile of 0
    values.
  * (b) "every indexed role … finds exactly one vertex": a role row on a dead slot. K32 survives. Control C7:
    `addRole(deck_end)` on the vertex (2000, 2000), then `flags |= VERTEX_FREE`.
  * (c) "no geometry carries a dead entity" through a face owner. The existing negative only kills a role row's entity.
    K33 survives. Control C8: `setOwner` of an L1 face to `block:dead`, with `isLive` false for it.
  * Required: add the three negatives.
* **B4 — simple-faces, C-0200 (4)'s "each hole ring clockwise or flat".** Neither the winding fixtures nor the fuzz runs
  ever see a hole ring wound counter-clockwise. K10 survives.
  * Control C3: an L2 island ring, with the host face's hole half-edges replaced by their twins
    (`setFaceHoles(…, holes.map(h => h ^ 1))`). The row fails, and holds under K10.
  * Required: add that negative.
* **B5 — prepared-contacts, "shared no finer edge".** C-0200 (13) says vacuous rows keep their predicates "built and
  tested", and §3.10 states this clause. K23 survives.
  * Control C9: an L1 way edge carrying an L2 `kerb` row, with `prepared: []`.
  * Required: add that negative.
